text:
ida: heads-up — seeing sustained KV cache growth on a dedicated pool when we feed long-context streams (30k+ tokens). Hosted runs with same model/seq pattern stabilize, but dedicated keeps climbing and triggers paging after ~2h. anyone seen similar?

mike: hmm, is this only on dedicated or also private (on-prem) pools?

ida: only Dedicated so far. Private on-prem runs show minor fragmentation but no steady leak. hosted is flat. dedicated config: a100-p4d, kernel 5.15, cgroups v2, jemalloc 5.3; using our default kvcache config (max_slots=256k, page_size=2M).

sophia: can you paste the pmap/perf snapshot? curious if pages are resident or swapped.

ida: quick dump attached below — long but relevant:
```
# pmap -x PID | tail -n 20
0000000000400000  4096K rw---   0K   0K anon
...
7f8a20000000  512M rw---  128M  64M kvcache-frames
7f8a24000000  1.5G rw---  1.2G 200M kvcache-frames
# vmstat 1 5
procs -----------memory---------- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ------cpu-----
 r  b   swpd   free   buff  cache   si   so    bi    bo   in   cs us sy id wa st
 0  0  123456  234M  12M  3.1G    0    0     0     5  120  210 30 10 55  5  0
```

ida: the interesting bit is that resident set slowly increases while swap stays low until a threshold; then we get sudden spike in pagefaults and eviction churn.

julien: any kernel journald or dmesg OOM lines? could be silent reclaim behavior. also dedicated nodes are on older NIC drivers — could be DMA-mapping differences that affect hugepage backing.

anita: reminder: Dedicated pools use a different tenant pinning policy and also have smaller OS page cache reserved via tuned profiles. That might change fragmentation patterns over long-allocation lifetimes.

mike: try toggling "kv_page_eviction_threshold" to a lower value for a day and see if steady growth stops. Also verify allocator stats from jemalloc (mallctl) — look for retained vs active.

ida: ran a quick jemalloc snapshot: retained ~1.8x active after 6 hours. active grows linearly with request count. attaching output: 
```
jemalloc stats:
allocated: 45G
active: 32G
retained: 58G
# arena_decay: 10s
```

sophia: that suggests fragmentation + pinned frames in kvcache. Are we coalescing free spans properly across page boundaries? Our kernel selection path for A100 runs picks a 2M-prefetch kernel, maybe misaligned with the hugepage settings on Dedicated.

julien: good call — hosted uses transparent hugepages off but dedicated had THP=always for perf reasons. THP can make small allocations occupy hugepage slots and increase internal fragmentation for kv slots. Try THP=never.

ida: switching THP to never on one node and re-running; will report in ~4h.

infra-bot: deploy-note: changed sysctl kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled from "always" to "never" on pool-dedicated-12 by ida at 3250004360.

mike: also confirm hugepage accounting: cat /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-2048kB/nr_hugepages and check hugetlb shmem usage. If kvcache expects smaller granularity but gets 2M pages, fragmentation visible.

ida: good catch — on the node nr_hugepages=0. so it's THP backing, not reserved hugetlb. initial run shows slower growth after THP flip, but still warm-up bump.

anita: could batch heuristics interact? Dedicated has more aggressive batching which keeps KV slots warm longer — that increases reuse but also retention. If a tiny percent of sessions keep unique context prefixes, the cache won't evict them with current LRUStrategy.

sophia: yep — LRUStrategy tuned for hosted's request pattern (many short sessions) doesn't match dedicated customers (fewer long sessions). We should add a 'session-ttl' or 'prefix-tenure' factor to eviction policy that decays slots not touched in N seconds, independent of total refcounts.

ida: quick profile from perf shows top callers during growth: 
```
# perf top -p PID
  12.0%  runtime.so  kvcache_insert
  9.1%   runtime.so  kv_lookup
  7.2%   libc-2.31   malloc
  5.5%   runtime.so  kvcache_evict_walk
```

mike: kvcache_evict_walk being expensive implies our eviction scan width is too large. For Dedicated we should reduce scan window or make it incremental background job. That would lower tail latency too.

julien: agree. proposal: add a config flag per pool: eviction_scan_limit=200 instead of global 2000, and enable background incremental compaction (throttle by cpu%). Make it opt-in for Dedicated.

ida: one more datapoint — private on-prem with cgroup v1 and kernel 6.2 had very different slab reuse; no user-visible growth. suspect kernel cgroup+OOM heuristics interplay.

sophia: action items so far:
- reproduce with THP toggled (ida)
- run jemalloc purged runs and collect retained/active hourly (mike)
- add per-pool eviction_scan_limit and run canary (julien)
- add session-ttl eviction prototype (sophia)

mike: I'll also instrument kv slot metadata with last_access_ts histogram to see long-tail reuse patterns. Low overhead metric (sample 1/1000) should be fine.

ida: thanks all — I’ll post results in a follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
